学者を志した青年が、権威への執着を手放し、会津の自然農法へたどり着くまで。SHI: How a young man who aspired to be a scholar let go of his attachment to authority and arrived at natural farming in Aizu. Why Kōta Uno, founder of SHINDO, calls this project a mission rather than a business.
FOUNDER'S NOTE ── 発起人の想い: FOUNDER'S NOTE ── Why I started this
かつて私は、学者を志しました。: I once set out to become a scholar.
世界は無知と狂気、そして権威と建前によってつくられており、世の中にある数々の問題: The world, I believed, was made of ignorance and madness, of authority and pretense, and the many problems in it would be solved once the right knowledge was found and spread by those with authority. Convinced of this, and determined to pursue society's right knowledge and reach a position of authority myself, I became a research assistant to a renowned management scholar, who was then 81.
それから二年が経ち、自分の中に二つの気づきが芽生えました。一つは、「真実」とは本: Two years later, two realizations had taken root in me. The first was that truth essentially lies dormant in the field, in reality itself, and that the right knowledge I had wanted could only be found by experiencing that reality directly and deeply. The second was that behind the pretext of wanting to change the world as a scholar, part of me had strongly craved authority itself.
現実世界では何が起きているのかを直接、直観しながら生きていきたい。そして、権威と: I wanted to live while sensing directly what was happening in the real world. I wanted to cast off my attachment to the ornament of authority, face reality as a participant on the ground, and live by the truths I perceived myself. I felt this strongly. Before long I left my job and began searching for a new way to live.
自らの言っていることと、やっていることを一致させる。世の中の潮流に押し流されず、: To bring what I say and what I do into line. To avoid being swept along by the currents of the age, to look again at the spiritual core that is my axis, and to live more freely and purely in pursuit of what is essential. And in doing so, to sharpen every sense and ability I was born with as a human being, and to explore what it means to be a more whole person. What kind of work could hold all of that?
この問いを抱えたまま一年が過ぎたころ、私は農業に出会いました。それから一年かけて: About a year into living with that question, I encountered farming. Over the following year I visited more than 30 natural and organic farms across Japan, and the last one I visited — Munokai Natural Farm, in the snow country of Aizu — I fell in love with at first sight. I moved there in the winter of 2021. It is a farming corporation that grows rice above all, along with soybeans, buckwheat, rapeseed oil, vegetables, and fruit, and has the largest area of organic rice cultivation in the prefecture.
それから三年。会津に限らず全国の地方を渡り、農業に携わるさまざまな人と話しをする: Three years on, traveling through rural regions well beyond Aizu and talking with all kinds of people involved in farming, something has come into view. The modern way of life we take for granted will not last much longer. Concretely: in the near future we will see a crisis in farming and food, the disappearance of rural communities, and the collapse of cities.
その原因の本質は、現代を生きる私たちの生き方と生活が、自然界、そして私たちの存在: The root cause, I constantly feel, is that the way we live today runs against the natural world and against the essence of our own existence. Yet I believe we adults have a duty to show the children who will create the next generation what it looks like to face such a turbulent future squarely and to live it fully, with a rich heart.
このプロジェクトはいわゆる「ビジネス」ではありません。私たちの意識をより本質的な: This project is not a business in the usual sense. It is a mission to shift our consciousness toward what is essential.
自らの「全て」をかけて、自らを含む世界のすべてを創り変えて参りますので、ご共感い: I will put everything I have into remaking the world, myself included. If any of this resonates with you, I ask for your support and your help.
